transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15 | Start: 14:00 PST | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Ivy (CSM), Devon (SE), Priya (Helix Head of ML), Liam (Helix Platform), Sofia (PM), Rajesh (Security)

[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: confirm cutover cadence, agree canary and A/B gates, monitoring/alerts, and next steps. Priya, do we still target the east coast region go-live in late January?
[00:18] Priya (Helix): Yeah the plan is still late Jan, but we need a clear rollback and a trial of the traffic shaping first. Our compliance team wants to see SLOs and audit hooks before any production traffic.
[00:33] Marco (Redwood): Totally. We're proposing a hybrid canary + A/B approach — start with 5% canary for 30 minutes, automated health checks, then expand with A/B cohorts at 10/90 split for quality comparison. If metrics break, immediate rollback to pinned model version.
[00:50] Liam (Helix): Quick q — how do you evaluate quality in the A/B? Is this automated or human review? We can't have product folks manually watch every request.
[01:05] Avery (Redwood): Good point. We recommend a mix: automated metric gating (BLEU-ish/embedding similarity, task-specific heuristics) plus sampled human review for the first 24h. We'll accept the customer-provided prompt sets for the automatic checks.
[01:23] Priya (Helix): We'll send the prompt sets. For ML gating we need delta thresholds; e.g., embedding similarity drop > 0.08 triggers alert, and top-1 accuracy drop > 3% triggers rollback.
[01:43] Marco (Redwood): We'll put those as configurable knobs in the runbook. Suggested automatic rollback triggers we discussed: error rate > 1% over 5m, p95 latency > 600ms for 10m, or model-quality delta above your thresholds.
[02:05] Sofia (Helix): Also want to confirm observability stack — we use Datadog and Sentry, and we want to see token-level cost breakdown in the dashboard.
[02:20] Devon (Redwood): We have integration guides; Marco will share the Datadog tracing snippet to correlate request IDs with Redwood traces. Token cost is available per-request in the console, and we'll add the per-route burn rate to the runbook.
[02:38] Rajesh (Helix): Security question — during canary we still need audit-logged keys and KMS-wrapped model artifacts. Can Redwood support bring-your-own-key for dedicated pools?
[02:52] Marco (Redwood): Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integration. For Hosted pilot we can enable customer-level encryption for payloads and keep audit logs. We'll share the security checklist.
[03:08] Priya (Helix): One more — what about prefix caching / KV cache behavior during canary? If cache warmness skews latency, we need deterministic testing.
[03:20] Marco (Redwood): Good call. We'll force cold-starts for the canary cohort in the dry run to measure baseline, and also document prefix/KV cache warming expectations. There's an option to disable KV caching for the canary if you want fully representative cold-latency.
[03:38] Avery (Redwood): Walk through the proposed cutover steps: prep window, dry-run in staging, non-business-hours dry-run with synthetic traffic, start 5% canary for 30 min, evaluate, expand to 25% if green, then A/B traffic 10/90 for quality comparison for 24 hours, then progressive rollout.
[03:58] Priya (Helix): What's the suggested rollback window? Immediate on trigger, but do you keep a safety window for humans to confirm?
[04:12] Marco (Redwood): Automatic rollback on critical triggers, but the runbook will include a 5-minute hold for manual override on degradations that are borderline. We'll log everything and send Slack/PagerDuty alerts.
[04:26] Liam (Helix): How do we route traffic? Feature flagging service + the Redwood routing policy? We want to integrate with LaunchDarkly.
[04:36] Devon (Redwood): Yes, we can route by header or LD flag. We'll provide the traffic-shift API and sample LaunchDarkly rules. For consistent experiments, we recommend deterministic hashing on user_id.
[04:52] Sofia (Helix): For the A/B quality comparisons, can we get side-by-side outputs and n-gram/delta metrics exported?
[05:03] Marco (Redwood): We'll export paired responses for sampling; the Redwood console can compute embedding-based similarity. We'll also give you a CSV with metrics per-prompt so you can plug into your QA dashboards.
[05:18] Priya (Helix): OK we'll want an SLA addendum for latency p95 and availability when we go fully live. Can we start negotiating that now?
[05:28] Avery (Redwood): We can start the enterprise SLA conversation — Redwood Dedicated contracts handle that. For pilot we'll include a service-level target in the runbook but formal SLA begins on Dedicated commit.
[05:42] Rajesh (Helix): About data residency — some PII pieces need to stay in our VPC region. Are there options for private deploy?
[05:51] Marco (Redwood): We support Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments; otherwise we can set region pinning and tenancy isolation. We'll share the tech spec for Private and the KMS integration guide.
[06:03] Sofia (Helix): Any concerns about cost spikes during A/B? Need to budget the token burn.
[06:11] Devon (Redwood): We'll run a cost simulation using your traffic profile and the selected quantization model. If cost is a concern we can recommend a int8/4 quantized variant to save 20-40% depending on workload.
[06:26] Priya (Helix): Cool. One operational question — who is on call during the dry run and cutover?
[06:33] Avery (Redwood): The runbook will include a contact matrix: Redwood on-call SE, AE escalation, and your platform lead. We'll also agree on a 2-hour blackout window for the dry-run.
[06:46] Liam (Helix): For testing, we'll need the reproducible benchmark script. Can Redwood provide the load generator config so our infra team can run 5,000 rps synthetic?
[06:58] Marco (Redwood): We'll share the JMeter/Gatling workload and the env variables. Note that synthetic traffic should include KV cache behavior if you want realistic token patterns.
[07:12] Priya (Helix): Let's set concrete numbers now to capture in the runbook: 5% canary for 30m -> gate -> 25% progressive for 2 hours -> A/B 10/90 for 24h -> full rollout. Rollback on error >1% for 5m, p95 latency >600ms for 10m, or quality delta as defined.
[07:40] Marco (Redwood): Got it — I'll encode those into the runbook along with the gating thresholds and the exact Grafana/Datadog dashboards to watch.
[07:52] Avery (Redwood): Other items — Ivy will coordinate the customer comms template for status updates, and we'll produce a one-page executive checklist for your stakeholders.
[08:04] Ivy (Redwood): I'll draft the comms and the incident template and share it to the Slack channel.
[08:15] Priya (Helix): Nice. Also want to validate the model pinning — we need immutable model versions and a fallback to the previous pinned hash.
[08:25] Marco (Redwood): Yes, Redwood supports model version pinning and instant fallback. We keep the model artifact hashes and allow immediate rollover to the prior model.
[08:38] Sofia (Helix): For the dry-run, we want a 'no-cache' and 'with-cache' run to measure variance.
[08:45] Marco (Redwood): We'll provide both. For the 'no-cache' run we'll ensure KV cache disabled for the canary cohort.
[08:56] Avery (Redwood): Ok let's recap and lock action items. We'll send the runbook draft + Datadog tracing snippet + benchmark CSV by Thursday. Helix will send prompt sets and run staging smoke tests. Schedule dry-run for week of 12/22.
[09:14] Priya (Helix): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:18] Avery (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up in thread with links. Meeting end.

Notes: transcript includes typical filler and occasional mis-transcription; some product names in convo may be shortened (e.g., 'Redwood Dedictated' was said). References shared: runbook draft (link to be provided), Datadog snippet (link), benchmark CSV (link).
